Remark. Interpretation: the squeeze mechanism behind the millennium bounds

Item (4) of the surreal rate calculus is the mechanism underlying every millennium-problem squeeze in Chapter 8 and Chapter 7: the "cost" of any standard-scale perturbation (a rogue zero off the critical line, a rogue vortex spike, a rogue Collatz trajectory, a rogue oracle separation) strictly exceeds the available mass-gap dissipation. The cost is transfinite, the dissipation is infinitesimal; no cancellation is possible in an ordered field.

This is the algebraic content that replaces the informal "O(\varepsilon^{-1}) exceeds O(\varepsilon^3) as \varepsilon \to 0": we do not need a limit, only an inequality inside \mathbf{No}.
